applies_to: Lochinvar Armor volume water heaters, models 1250-4000, Series 100 and 101, with the SMART SYSTEM control and the Modbus/BACnet communication board.
summary: The large Armor water heaters (1250-4000 MBH) talk BACnet MS/TP through Lochinvar's add-on Modbus/BACnet communication board. The fixed object map has two writable binary values (enable and tank thermostat), safety-switch and output status inputs, temperatures, firing rate, status/blocking/lockout codes, cascade totals, and analog values the BAS writes for configuration, rate or setpoint, tank setpoint and tank temperature.
notes: BACnet needs the optional communication board; its address and baud rate are set on dip switches.
The board is an MS/TP master only, so MAC addresses 0-127 are usable.
AV 0 (Configuration) is a bitmask: setting a bit tells the heater to use the BAS-written value instead of its own input.
AI 0-2 and AI 25 pack the binary inputs into 16-bit words.
Temperatures are in °C on the bus.
Revision C of this manual changed the analog-value table; earlier revisions list different analog values.

source.title: Modbus and BACnet Communication Instructions, Armor Models 1250-4000, Series 100 & 101

integration.summary: Set parameter H5 ModBus to Active on the SMART SYSTEM control, then write AV 0 Configuration so the heater knows which values the BAS will supply. After that the BAS sends an enable (BV 0 / AV 1), a rate or setpoint command (AV 2), or both, and keeps rewriting them. Status, temperatures and the status, blocking and lockout codes can be read without taking control.

integration.enable: Set H5 ModBus = Active. Enable only (local setpoints): AV 0 = 0x0001 and AV 1 Coils = 1 (0 disables). Enable plus rate: AV 0 = 0x0005, AV 1 = 1 and AV 2 = modulation % or setpoint. Rate only: AV 0 = 0x0004 and AV 2. AV 2 is a firing % or a setpoint depending on the BMS Type setting; as a setpoint it is scaled like a 0-10 V signal between the BMS temperatures set for the low and high analog input.
integration.heartbeat: BAS-written tank temperature and the 0-10 V/rate value must be refreshed every few seconds; parameter H6 ModBus Time sets the timeout (the manual gives 5-120 s with a 10 s default in one place and 1-255 s in another). Other commands such as the enable have a fixed 4-minute timeout. When either timer runs out the heater goes back to its local inputs.
integration.remote_sensors: Set the AV 0 bits for the values the BAS will supply, then write AV 3 tank setpoint and/or AV 4 tank temperature (°C). The tank temperature must be rewritten every few seconds or the heater returns to its own sensor.
setup: MAC address from dip switches 1-8 (master only, so 0-127); baud from switches 9-10: 9600, 19200, 38400 or 76800.
RS-485 bus up to 4000 ft, 24 AWG shielded twisted pair, 120 ohm termination at each end, up to 32 nodes.
gotchas: The manual says to resend the AV 0 configuration bits before each command.
In a cascade only the leader needs the board for control; it then reports cascade totals only, so fit a board to every unit to see each one.
Without H5 set to Active the board is monitor-only.
The lockout code changes during normal operation; read it only when the status code is 40.
